The ASV writes touch no hallowed thing with no word for this preposition's relation (rule 40).

The single no carries both the clause negation and the universal quantifier, so the two morphemes share one unit across the intervening noun, exactly as Nor carries coordination and negation (rules 30, 35); headed on the negative. The competing reading gives no to לֹא alone and marks כֹּל unrepresented (rule 8).

review_notes: Two determiner questions carry the verse: the first italic her (t009) is added because טָהֳרָה is bare there, while the second her (t030) answers to a written suffix.
The no of touch no hallowed thing is read as a fusion of כֹּל with לֹא; the alternative of giving it to לֹא alone and leaving כֹּל unrepresented is named in that unit's note.
